pusillanimous

pyoo-suh-LAN-uh-muhs · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Pusillanimous is lacking courage or determination.

Historians called the general's decision to retreat without a fight pusillanimous, a stain on an otherwise proud military career.

Worked Example

The board's pusillanimous refusal to confront the failing CEO cost the company another two years of losses.

Being too cowardly to make a difficult but necessary decision is exactly what pusillanimous describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

timid: Timid describes a shy, easily frightened temperament, and it carries no moral judgment -- a timid child is protected, not blamed. Pusillanimous is an accusation: it condemns a person or a decision as shamefully lacking the courage a situation demanded.

weak-willed: Weak-willed means unable to hold to a decision or resist temptation -- the diet dropped by Friday, the resolution abandoned at the first excuse. It is a failure of willpower, not of nerve. Pusillanimous is a failure of courage: too fearful to face a risk or a hard duty, and shamefully so.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

courageous: able to face danger or difficulty with bravery

bold: confident and willing to take risks

Where it sits · how complete the failure of courage — cowardly → pusillanimous → spineless

cowardly vs. pusillanimous: Cowardly is milder than pusillanimous: slipping out the back door once is a cowardly lapse, while a pusillanimous person shows a deeper, more complete failure of courage in everything.

spineless vs. pusillanimous: Spineless is harsher than pusillanimous: a pusillanimous manager lacks courage, but calling him spineless goes further, saying he caves to every complaint and never defends his own staff.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — pusill-

root — pusill-: very small, weak (Latin)

root — anim-

root — anim-: spirit, mind, soul (Latin)

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: full of, having the quality of (Latin (-osus))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin pusillus ('very small, petty') plus animus ('spirit, mind') plus -ous ('having the quality of') -- pusillanimous literally means 'small-spirited,' too weak-spirited to face danger or make a hard choice.

Use the root in a new word: unanimous

Root Check

Word Choice

Pusillanimous is a strong, almost scornful word -- reserve it for judging a decision or a person's character as shamefully cowardly, not just for describing ordinary nervousness. Compare it with timorous, which describes fearfulness itself rather than a moral failing, and diffident, which is about social self-doubt rather than fear of danger at all.
